perception_gap_frames.topic: Press freedom signals need careful reading
perception_gap_frames.frame_text:
Media/comms view: cbsnews.com and aljazeera.com focused on information access, audience exposure, platform effects, press freedom, and narrative spread.
State/policy view: wider regional and policy coverage focused more on official positioning, regulation, sanctions, security claims, and state interests.
The gap: one frame shows how information may reach or shape audiences; the other shows how authorities or institutions are trying to define the event.
Why it matters: a reader who only sees the official frame may miss how the story is being distributed, restricted, or reframed for audiences.

observations.title: Press-freedom coverage describes operating climate
observations.body: A press-freedom story becomes part of the operating climate when it changes access, safety, censorship, legal pressure, or source reliability.

observations.title: Regulation matters when it changes reach
observations.body: Regulation becomes a media-company issue when it changes who can publish, distribute, monetise, or access information.

observations.title: Narrative risk depends on spread
observations.body: The practical difference is claim versus channel. A false or state-linked narrative matters more when it moves across platforms or audiences, not just because one outlet names it.

observations.title: Sanctions coverage needs practical interpretation
observations.body: Sanctions coverage matters when changing rules affect who can operate, publish, transact, travel, or distribute.
